To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) GWAS identified markers associated with GY in SWW and the effects of the markers were confirmed in a Mexican spring wheat panel; 2) the TP size and covariate addition had a positive effect on the prediction accuracy of GS in SWW; and 3) combining phenotypic with GS resulted in higher genetic gains than GS alone.

1) Genome wide association study (GWA) identified markers associated with grain yield (GY), plant height (PH), kernel weight (KW), and test weight (TW), and 2) Genomic selection (GS) was superior to marker assisted selection and combining GS with phenotypic selection increased genetic gain in wheat breeding programs

(1) GWAS and GS can be used to increase genetic gains and accelerate wheat breeding programs; and (2) GS is superior to MAS and can be combined with phenotypic selection for higher genetic gain in wheat breeding programs.
